szoveg_eredeti:
The best image to video AI tool in 2026 depends on what you want to animate. For cinematic shots from a still, the strongest models are Kling 4.0, Seedance 2.5, Veo 3.1 and MiniMax H3. You can use each one in its own app, or run several of them side by side in a multi-model tool like Krea. If you want a talking photo, where a portrait speaks a script, HeyGen is built for that job. For a few free clips a day, Google Flow gives everyone 50 credits daily, which is about five Veo 3.1 Lite clips.

This guide compares ten image to video (also called photo to video) AI tools: free allowance, cheapest paid plan, longest clip, and whether you can set both a start and an end frame. We pulled every number from the vendor’s own pages on 2026-10-29 and link the source. Prices and free credits in this category change monthly, so check the links before you buy. Krea is our product. We say where it wins and where it doesn’t.

Upload a photo once, then try Kling 4.0, Seedance 2.5, Veo 3.1, MiniMax H3 and Wan 3.0 on it in the same workspace.

Every price, credit count and clip length comes from a vendor page we opened on 2026-10-29: Krea pricing, Kling’s image to video page and membership page, Google Flow’s credits help page and model guide, Runway pricing, Adobe Firefly plans, Luma pricing, Pika pricing, HeyGen pricing, Hailuo and Vidu pricing. When a vendor did not publish a number, the table says so instead of guessing. Clip lengths for models we run on Krea come from Krea’s own model settings. This post makes no quality ranking. Motion quality changes with every model release, so the fair test is your own image on two or three of these.

Four things decide whether a tool works for you:

Krea is a multi-model AI image and video platform. For image to video, you upload a photo (or generate one with Krea 3) and choose from more than 20 video models. These are the main ones and their limits on Krea today:

The practical advantage is comparison. You can run the same still through three models, keep the best take, then extend it or upscale it to 4K with the video upscaler. Krea Agent can plan a multi-shot sequence from one brief and pick models for you.

Pricing, from krea.ai/pricing on 2026-10-29: the Free plan gives 100 compute units a day with Krea 3 images and Krea Agent. The pricing page marks video access on Free as limited and says Seedance needs a paid plan. On video, Free can run LTX-2 19B, Hailuo 2.3 Fast and, while a MiniMax promotion lasts, MiniMax H3. Only LTX-2 19B fits the daily allowance: a 5-second 512p clip costs 34 units, so 100 units cover about two clips a day. One Hailuo 2.3 Fast clip (141 units for 6 seconds at 768p) or MiniMax H3 clip (481 units for 5 seconds) costs more than a day’s free units. Basic is $5/month billed yearly ($9 monthly) with 5,000 units, which the page puts at about 15 Seedance 2.0 Fast videos, plus selected video models. Pro is $21/month billed yearly ($35 monthly) with 20,000 units and all video models, including Seedance 2.5. Paid plans include a commercial license.

Where Krea stops: free video is limited to about two short 512p LTX-2 clips a day, and each model keeps its own limits (Veo 3.1 tops out at 8 seconds on Krea, as it does everywhere). Krea has no avatar library or talking-photo presenter tool. Its lip sync tool animates a portrait to an audio track with VEED Fabric or Hedra, but HeyGen goes further for presenter video.

Kling is Kuaishou’s video model family, and Kling 4.0 is its current flagship. Per Kling’s image to video page, “the full Kling 4.0 model supports video generation from 3 to 30 seconds per clip,” output goes “up to 4K,” and you can set “start and end frames or use up to 10 flexible keyframes.” Kling 3.0 is still offered for clips up to 15 seconds.

Pricing: paid plans on the membership page list Standard at $10/month with 660 credits, Pro at $37 with 3,000, Premier at $207 with 18,000, and Ultra+ at $619 with 57,000, before a running first-month discount and a 34% yearly discount. Paid plans include watermark removal, 1080p/4K and commercial use. The free tier gives daily login credits, but Kling does not publish the amount. Its FAQ says “watermark-free downloads may require a paid plan” and that commercial use falls under paid membership terms.

Where Kling stops: one model family only, and the free allowance is unpublished and changes with promotions. Kling 4.0 also runs on Krea at up to 30 seconds and 1080p.

Google’s Flow is the most generous free route to a frontier model. Google’s help page says “with or without a subscription, you receive 50 Google Flow credits per day.” A Veo 3.1 Lite generation costs 10 credits for non-Ultra users, so a free day is about five Lite clips. Veo 3.1 Fast costs 20 credits and Veo 3.1 Quality costs 100, so Quality is out of reach on free credits alone. Clips are 4, 6 or 8 seconds, and “Frames to Video: First and last” works on Lite, Fast and Quality.

Pricing: Google AI Plus ($4.99/month) adds 200 Flow credits a month, and AI Pro ($19.99/month) adds 1,000. 1080p upscaling is free for subscribers; 4K upscaling is Ultra only.

Where Flow stops: 8 seconds maximum. Google also says non-subscribers may be blocked from video “during peak hours, roughly 2 PM to 5 PM UTC.” Unused daily credits don’t carry over.

Runway builds its own models (Gen-4.5, Gen-4 Turbo, Aleph 2.0) and now also hosts Kling 4.0, Seedance 2.0 and 2.5, and others. Gen-4.5 supports image to video. Runway’s page says “Gen-4.5 uses 12 credits per second,” so a 5-second clip costs 60 credits.

Pricing on 2026-10-29: the Free plan gives 125 one-time credits. Standard is $12/month billed yearly ($15 monthly) with 625 credits, which Runway equates to ”52s of Gen-4.5.” Pro is $28 yearly ($35 monthly) with 2,250 credits, and Max is $76 yearly ($95 monthly) with 9,500 credits that roll over one month. Paid plans have no watermark.

Where Runway stops: the free credits are one-time, and Standard’s 625 credits come to under a minute of Gen-4.5. On Krea, Runway Gen-4.5 takes a start frame and runs 2 to 10 seconds.

Firefly does image to video with Adobe’s own Firefly Video Model and partner models, including Veo 3.1 Fast, Runway Gen-4.5, Kling 3.0 and Luma. Adobe says output goes “up to 4K,” clips run “approximately five seconds (depending on AI model used),” and you can add an end frame. It also states that Firefly “does not add a watermark to any videos you generate.”

Pricing: the free plan includes “free daily generations across image, video, and audio.” Firefly Standard is $9.99/month for 2,000 generative credits (up to 20 five-second videos), Pro $19.99 for 4,000, and Pro Plus $49.99 for 10,000. Credits don’t roll over.

Where Firefly stops: short clips on the Firefly model, and a partner-model list that trails the newest releases (Kling 3.0, not 4.0, on the page we checked).

Luma makes the Ray models. Ray 3.2 does text to video and image to video in 5- or 10-second clips from 360p to 1080p, with HDR and EXR export options aimed at post-production. Luma also hosts Seedance 2.0 and 2.5, Kling 4.0 and 3.0, Veo 3.1, MiniMax H3 and FLUX 3.

Pricing: Plus is $30/month for 10,000 credits, Pro $90 for 40,000, Ultra $300 for 150,000. Ray 3.2 at 1080p costs 400 credits per 5 seconds, so Plus covers about 25 such clips. The page lists no standing free plan, only “free trial credits.”

Where Luma stops: no free tier and a high entry price. On Krea, Luma Ray 3.2 runs 5 or 10 seconds with start and end frames.

Pika is built for playful, effect-driven clips: Pikaffects, Pikaframes (keyframe transitions) and its own Pika 2.5 model. It also offers Seedance 2.5, MiniMax H3, Wan 3.0 and Gemini Omni Flash.

Pricing: the Free plan is “0 credits / month · packs only.” You can buy credit packs, output has no watermark, but the commercial license is “No.” Starter is $8/month billed yearly ($10 monthly) for 900 credits, and Creator $28 yearly ($35 monthly) for 3,150. Seedance 2.5 at 720p for 5 seconds costs 122 credits.
